summary: Tetsuhiko Shibata is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University under Eijun Hattori, Yukan Ozawa, and Mitsuo Sato. He served as a lecturer in Jodo studies at Taisho University.

Tetsujiro Inoue (1856–1944) was a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who studied at the University of Tokyo, Heidelberg University, and Leipzig University. He held posts at the University of Tokyo (1882) and Toyo University (circa 1925–1944).

Tetsuo Otani (born 1939) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda and Komazawa universities. He held academic positions at Komazawa, Tomakomai Komazawa, Tsuru, and Tohoku Fukushi universities, as well as Peking University.
Tetsuo Suzuki (born 1934) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology. He studied at Shizuoka University until around 1957 and served as an assistant professor at Otani University.

Tetsuro Watsuji (1889–1960) was a philosopher, religious studies scholar, and Japanologist who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Toyo, Hosei, Kyoto, Otani, Ryukoku, and the University of Tokyo, where he chaired Ethics.

Tetsushi Furukawa (1912–2011) specialized in philosophy and Japanology, studying at the University of Tokyo from circa 1933 to 1937. He held academic posts at the University of Tokyo (circa 1950–1973), Asia University, and International Budo University.
Thanon Chitkament is a history and archaeology scholar who studied under guide V. D. Gogte and co-guide P. S. Joshi.

Theodor Aufrecht (1822–1907) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin. He held posts at Berlin, Oxford, the University of Edinburgh as Professor of Sanskrit, and the University of Bonn as Professor.

Theodor Benfey (1809–1881) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Göttingen from circa 1824 to 1829. He served as a teacher (Lehrmeister) at the University of Göttingen from 1834 to 1881.

Theodor Bloch (1867–1909) was a scholar of Indology and archaeology. He studied at Leipzig University under Ernst Windisch (circa 1888–1893) and under Georg Bühler as a special student (circa 1894–1895).

Theodor Goldstücker (1821–1872) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Peter von Bohlen, Karl Rosenkranz, Christian Lassen, and Eugène Burnouf. He was Professor of Sanskrit at the University of London and taught at University College London.

Theodor Nöldeke (1836–1930) was a linguist and Iranian/Central Asian studies scholar who studied at Göttingen under Theodor Benfey, Vienna, Berlin, and Leiden. He held posts at the universities of Göttingen, Kiel, and Strasbourg.
Theodore Dwight Woolsey (1801–1889) was a scholar in linguistics, history, and archaeology. He was educated at Hopkins School and studied at Yale College from circa 1816 to 1820.

Theodore Gabriel is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. He completed an M.Litt. at the University of Aberdeen and served as a Lecturer in Religious Studies at the University of Gloucestershire.

Theodore Stcherbatsky (1866–1942) was an Indologist, Buddhologist, and philosopher who studied under Ivan Pavlovich Minaev, Georg Bühler, and Hermann Jacobi. He served as a member of the Russian Academy of Sciences from circa 1918 to 1942.
Theophil Gubler was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied under Jacob Wackernagel and completed his doctoral degree at the University of Basel in 1903.
Thich Nhat Hanh (1926–2022) was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. Between 1961 and 1963, he studied and taught at both Columbia University and Princeton University.
Thich Thien Nghiem is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Delhi in 2012, where he studied under doctoral supervisor Shalini Singhal and teacher K. T. S. Sarao.

Thierry Mathou (born 1963) is a history, archaeology, and Tibetology scholar. He studied at EDHEC Business School and the Paris Institute of Political Studies, and served as an Associated Political Scientist at the CNRS.

Thierry Meynard (born 1963) is a sinologist and philosopher who earned his PhD at Peking University under Yulie Lou. He served as Professor of Philosophy at Sun Yat-sen University and director of The Beijing Center for Chinese Studies.
